items.detail: The **Nasdaq** rose 0.8% to 25,372.01 Tuesday and the S&P 500 gained about 0.4% to 7,567.72, ending a three-day losing streak for both.
items.why: Chip stocks bounced nearly 3%, though Apple's 2% drop on a weak margin forecast held the Dow back.

items.detail: That rebound reversed overnight: **Nasdaq-100 futures** fell as much as 2.2% as Democrats looked set to win both the House and the Senate.
items.why: Traders expect a Democratic Congress to slow the build-out of AI data centers and scrutinize tech more closely.

items.detail: **AMD** rose as much as 7% after hours, a rare bright spot after a 23% slide over the past month, with Friday's payrolls next.
items.why: AMD forecast faster-than-expected growth in 2027 as sales of its data-center chips surge.

items.detail: South Korea's **Kospi** fell another 3.2% to 5,466.83 Wednesday, a second straight heavy drop, and Taiwan and Japan also slid sharply.
items.why: Early Democratic midterm wins revived fears of tighter rules on AI, hitting SK Hynix and Samsung again.

items.detail: The **Nifty** rose 1.58% to 23,810.85 Tuesday, its fourth straight gain and highest close in nearly two months, then opened higher again Wednesday.
items.why: Foreign buying and softer crude kept the rally going, though gains are concentrated in Reliance and a few large stocks.

items.detail: The US **Russell 2000** edged up only 0.23% to 2,812.45 Tuesday, well behind the Nasdaq's chip-led bounce, before US futures slid overnight.
items.why: Small caps got little from the chip rebound, and election-night selling is now pulling the whole US market lower.

items.detail: **Bitcoin** briefly fell to about $75,700, a two-month low, as midterm results came in, then recovered to near $76,700.
items.why: Bets on a Democratic sweep raised fears of tougher crypto rules and a stalled CLARITY Act.

items.detail: **Ether** slipped 0.75% to about **$2,234**, below the $2,260 level it had been holding and closer to last week's post-hack low.
items.why: Fears of a Democratic Congress added to Monday's $139.8 million in outflows from US spot ether ETFs.

items.detail: **Solana** fell 1.62% to about **$90.45**, sliding further below the $100 level it broke last week.
items.why: Election-driven regulation fears and lingering worry over the Binance hack forced long bets to sell.

items.detail: **Gold** rose 0.5% to $3,947.49 Wednesday, regaining Tuesday's 0.5% loss but still below $4,000.
items.why: The dollar and Treasury yields fell as Democrats won early races, making non-yielding gold more attractive.

crossCuttingTheme: Democrats' midterm gains are the new driver: bets on tighter rules for tech and crypto are hitting chip stocks from Nasdaq futures to Seoul and Tokyo and pushing bitcoin lower, while a weaker dollar and lower yields are lifting gold.
